narrative:
The model estimated a 51.0% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above even, but it crossed the threshold used in this review, so your law school application was denied. This is a risk estimate, not a certainty.

The denial was driven most strongly by your third-year class-rank decile. You are in the first decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile, and this factor pushed the prediction toward bar failure. The second most important factor was your low family-income bracket, which pushed toward passing; it was therefore a protective signal, even though low-income students are rare among accepted applicants. The third factor was your first-year decile, also first, compared with an accepted average near the sixth decile; it likewise pushed toward failure. Together, the two very low class-rank signals outweighed the protective income signal.

Your next step should be to ask admissions whether an appeal or reconsideration is possible and what evidence would help, such as context for your rankings or a plan for academic support. In parallel, consider retaking the LSAT, strengthening your academic record, and applying to programs with holistic review.
